# Chapter 18 finite contract

- `query-corpus.json`: independently authored expected result, gap, evidence, pair and IOC fields for 40 finite inputs. QCASE18-01–40 each has a requirement owner. The 12 published HCASE18 rows identify their corresponding QCASE18 input. Do not replace expected values with values generated by the implementation under test.
- `publication-contract.json`: authored Layer A checkpoints, closed schema/corpus byte digests, parent byte digests, source identity and exact shared-projection field inventories for four complete documents. The Case displays every Artifact leaf except the raw query input; the input is supplied in the linked JSON. No chapter-specific Markdown grammar is implemented.
- `scripts/chapter18_query.py`: fixed synthetic consent/use question, version 1.0.0. Fictional integer offsets, bounded populations, three supplied coverage assertion streams. Not a SIEM, arbitrary query language, real collector validator, authorization grant or incident classifier.
- `scripts/chapter18_model.py`: fixed authored input, supply evidence bindings, judgments and undelivered handoffs.
- `scripts/check_chapter18_contract.py`: complete surface selection, shared Publication Projection 1.1.0 and Content Safety Policy 1.2.0 consumption, parent/source/route ownership.
- `scripts/chapter18_regressions.py`: fixed counterexamples, finite input orders, coverage removal, closed object keys, evidence and handoff mutation with authored hashes refreshed to isolate semantic checks, publication preamble/body/tail/heading/inventory and provenance cardinality tests, strict JSON and bounded local-file tests.

## Exact host provenance exceptions

Eleven exact field identities (type, element, attribute, heading level, text and location) are reviewed as non-target provenance: version prose for ATT&CK 19.2 and Python 3.12, the fixed local checker command, the registered cross-book delegate link, ATT&CK version/update/strategy links and version prose, and NIST Final/version/PDF provenance. The shared host scanner currently recognizes some version/path-like text as host tokens. These are not wildcard URL/host or paragraph-prefix permissions.

Each exception must occur exactly once. Changed, moved, duplicated or extended fields fail the frozen contract. The action scanner always runs, including on host-exempt fields. No exception applies to JSON inputs. New prose or provenance requires explicit review; do not automatically collect current scanner findings into the exception list to silence failures. Issue #67 and shared Policy grammar remain separate and unchanged.

## Maintenance and limits

Use the existing pinned renderer and whole-document projection to inspect a deliberate editorial change, review each typed field, then update the authored checkpoint in the same reviewed change. There is no production command that learns current output as expected output. Query changes require independently reviewed expected results; changing a digest alone does not discharge the semantic tests. Parent digests intentionally fail on unrelated parent changes until their effect is reviewed.

Run `python3 scripts/check_chapter18_contract.py`, with PYTHONHASHSEED 0, 1, 7 and 42 for release checks. Stable ordering comes from fixed inventories and sorted evidence/pairs/gaps; order and deduplication are asserted. Standard-library tests do not claim an OS sandbox. Bounded static Linux/WSL2 file checks reject symlinks, directories and FIFOs but are not a hostile concurrent filesystem security boundary. All runtime scratch directories stay under the repository's ignored `.work/`.

Supply receipts are educational assumptions, not actual collection evidence. The fixed JSON representation hash identifies the supplied input; it does not prove authenticity. Parent Chapter 16/17 data, states, evidence, permissions and undelivered handoffs are not inherited. Unsupported inputs fail closed; unsupported general renderer syntax remains owned by the shared projection module.
